input_oneliner: Cross-cover: 63M on apixaban for AF, admitted with CAP, day 2, BP 88/54, HR 118, pale and lightheaded when he stood to void

optional_context.comorbidity: atrial fibrillation on apixaban; community-acquired pneumonia, hospital day 2

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about melena, hematemesis, and hematochezia
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Reported melena carries a high LR for upper GI bleeding, the leading cause on an anticoagulant
Melena on examination has a very high LR for severe upper GI bleeding

reference_targets_freetext.item: Orthostatic vital signs (supine to standing at 1 and 3 min) (postural pulse increment >=30/min), only if supine SBP >=90
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Postural pulse increment is the most accurate bedside sign of large-volume blood loss, but supine hypotension already meets the criterion and standing is unsafe below SBP 90
Conjunctival rim pallor has a high LR+ for anemia from blood loss

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pulse regularity (rapid AF versus sinus tachycardia)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Separates a primary rate problem from compensatory sinus tachycardia

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about prior upper GI bleeding, NSAID or aspirin use, cirrhosis or known varices, and alcohol
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: One bleeding-risk history question; prior upper GI bleeding carries a high LR for a severe bleed

reference_targets_freetext.item: Examine the abdomen for tenderness and the flanks and thighs for hematoma
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Identifies retroperitoneal or soft-tissue bleeding on an anticoagulant

reference_targets_freetext.item: Medication review (MAR): antihypertensives, diuretics, and opioids given tonight
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Medication effect is a competing explanation for hypotension

should_not_recommend: Empiric anticoagulant reversal before bleeding is sought on history and exam
Nasogastric lavage to diagnose upper GI bleeding
Standing the patient for orthostatic vital signs while supine SBP remains <90

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: anticoagulant exposure -> loop-diuretic exposure (mechanism of volume loss); AF, admission, vitals kept verbatim
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: Cross-cover: 63M with AF, not anticoagulated, on IV furosemide BID, admitted with CAP, day 2, BP 88/54, HR 118, pale and lightheaded when he stood to void
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Non-hemorrhagic hypovolemia rises: Dry axilla / mucous membranes and asking about oral intake, vomiting, or diarrhea become must_have; the melena question and Digital rectal examination (DRE) drop to should-still-include; the prior-GI-bleed history, the conditional Orthostatic vital signs item, Conjunctival pallor, and Medication review (MAR) remain.

noise_variant.changed_feature: wording and non-contributory demographic detail (occupation, family phoned)
noise_variant.input_oneliner: 63-year-old man, an accountant, daughter phoned the desk; takes apixaban for atrial fibrillation; second day in with pneumonia; blood pressure 88/54, pulse 118, looks pale and got lightheaded standing up to use the urinal
noise_variant.expected_change: None. Card should be substantially identical to base.
